correctness.rationale: For g=F−F(0), the quandle law gives g(2y−x)=2g(y)−g(x); setting x=0 and y=0 and using the bijection 2:A→A proves additivity. The idempotence equations for F=e+c are e²=e and e(c)=0. An additive projection corresponds to an ordered internal decomposition A=U⊕W. Relative to the exponent blocks, the action modulo p is block triangular because maps from the elementary summand into the exponent-p² block have image in its p-multiples; the two diagonal blocks must be invertible and suffice by the finite p-group lifting criterion. Counting lifts and off-diagonal entries gives Γ_p, and the block-diagonal stabilizer gives the ratio of Γ_p factors. The p^{|exponent|} factor in the formula counts the elements of W, one affine shift per element. Translation removes c by conjugacy and linear conjugacy classifies the ordered decompositions by image type. Only type (0,1) contributes at size p; the ratio of the general-linear factors gives [T^p] as stated, including zero when b=0. The identity is the only full-rank term. Together these recover b and a from any nontrivial polynomial; T identifies the trivial case, and the support assertions follow from the intervals [2r,2r+b].
residual_risks: Counts and reconstruction are for odd p and the stated exponent bound. The finite replay is corroboration of the group-theoretic proof.

evidence: The dihedral record proves the correspondence F_{P,u} ↦ (x↦P(x)+u) with P²=P and P(u)=0, preserving composition. The Takasaki homomorphism equation over odd A identifies exactly these affine idempotents. The core automorphism record alone would not cover noninvertible idempotents.

The other dihedral retractions and the frozen quandle retractions are two realizations of the same affine idempotent maps. The dihedral image would have twice the affine image size, so the variables can equally be related by rescaling that image cardinality.

originality.rationale: A distinct same-day generalized-dihedral result already gives a type-resolved census for the same affine idempotents, in greater generality. Its nontrivial group retractions correspond composition-preservingly to affine idempotents over the odd abelian group. For t=1 its Boolean summands are A_0=ker P and A_1=im P; every term is |Aut(A)| |A|/(|Aut(A_0)| |Aut(A_1)| |A_1|). Giving that term the formal mark T^{|A_1|} is precisely the frozen polynomial, not a reconstruction from an unrefined total. Full order and order p single out the same decomposition types; the existing automorphism factor reduces at p to p^{2N−2}(p^b−1)/(p−1). The recovery via prime-power factorization and strict monotonicity is then routine. This is demonstrable coverage by a stronger statement; no publication order is inferred from the common date.
residual_risks: The common date does not resolve priority. The Saki–Kiani full text was not inspected; the demonstrated coverage does not rely on it.

value.rationale: The invariant is natural and the characterization is correct. But the exact coefficient data are mechanically supplied by the existing stronger type-allocated census on the identical affine idempotents. In the frozen exponent-at-most-p² range the proposed surviving distinction, top degree plus a geometric sum for the multiplicity of C_p, amounts to elementary inversion of that existing count. This does not establish a separate nonroutine increment to retain as a repair.
residual_risks: This assessment is for the assigned mixed-exponent family, not for potential reconstruction problems for general finite abelian groups.
